judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration recital; the only oddities ('te', trailing ':.') are OCR artifacts rather than meaning-changing errors. Nothing in it that two parties could read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply introduces the Discovery Period Activation amendments and is consistent with Section III and the Declarations Item 4 premium mechanics. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference is garbled ('Section XDI' for Section XIII), but the operative content — termination at 12:01 a.m. on 05/13/2009 — is a precise date with no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The date matches the amended Policy Period in the Change Policy Period endorsement (c020) and the Discovery Period effective date, so the instrument hangs together on timing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer sentence ('Subject to all provisions set forth in Section III') introducing a table; the reference is garbled but its sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The table it introduces shows retentions and limits that do not line up exactly with Declarations Items 8 and 9 (e.g., a $160,000 D&O figure), which could raise a question about which retention governs Discovery Period claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Legally permitted to indemnify ... regardless of whether actual indemnification is granted' is a deeming rule whose application to an acquiring entity's indemnification law could be argued, though the words are reasonably tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Section VII(B)(2) but substitutes 'the acquiring entity' for 'the Company', which sits awkwardly with Section VII(B)(1)(a)'s no-retention rule when no indemnification is legally available.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wrongful Acts involving the entity or entities set forth in Item 1' is a vague limiter — 'involving' has no defined boundary — and the clause folds the acquiring entity into 'Company' only partially.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Section IV(E) (c042), which was expressly 'subject to Section XII (B)', while the same endorsement deletes Section XII entirely (c006), leaving the scope of 'Company' during the Discovery Period contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion; its own words are unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleting Section XII leaves live cross-references elsewhere — Section IV(E) 'subject to Section XII (B)', Exclusion V(O)'s 'except as provided in Section XII (C)(3)', and the Fiduciary endorsement's Insured definition 'acquired ... pursuant to Section XII' — creating dangling references.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, definite statement that the Discovery Period premium is fully earned; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats Section III's identical fully-earned language, so it harmonises rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective-date statement with no interpretive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 05/13/2009 date coincides with the policy termination date in c002 and the Discovery Period effective date in the table, which is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard endorsement savings language; 'other than as above stated' cabins it clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the other endorsements' identical savings clauses and does not undo the amendments it accompanies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain-language notice about claims-made, no-duty-to-defend and defense-costs erosion; each statement is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section IX(A)(1) and the Limit of Liability provisions; the only faint tension is with the non-erosion provision in Section VIII(A).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single aggregate figure of $10,000,000; the OCR-mangled word 'paovises' does not change the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The separate Insuring Agreement limits in Item 8 total well over $10,000,000, so the Total Policy Limit's interplay with Section VII(A)(1)-(3) and Item 7 could be argued, though Section VII(A)(1) expressly harmonises them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Percentage and 365-day length are stated numerically; 'if the eligibility requirements are met' points outward but is not itself vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section III supplies the eligibility requirements and the same multiplication formula, and the premiums actually charged match 75%, so it coheres.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mailing address and phone number; nothing capable of two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section X(C) points to this Item and the address is consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear condition: no coverage unless limit, retention and premium are shown.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the Section I preamble (c031); the only friction is that Insuring Agreement A shows a '$0' retention and 'N/A' entries appear in the separate-limit column.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence bundles four coverages into Insuring Agreement (C) and then conditions their exclusion on a 'different Limit of Liability or retention' being 'desired', a subjective and undated trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Securities Liability Exclusion endorsement (c124) and separate Securities Liability Insuring Agreement (c165) cut across this bundling, so whether securities claims sit in (C) or only in Form 5098 is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes a $5,000 retention and then, in the next sentence, subjects endorsement-provided IRA/Keogh coverage to the Item 9 retention, which reads as two different answers depending on how coverage is delivered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to 'Section IV (X)(2)' and to Insuring Agreement (C) ties into Section VII(A)(4)'s reinstatement, but no IRA/Keogh coverage is actually scheduled, leaving the provision partly inoperative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of endorsement form numbers ends in unreadable characters ('500! | 5 0€ > aH'), so the set of incorporated endorsements cannot be read off the face of the item.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The later Declarations amendments (c021, c026) list different endorsement sets, so which endorsements form part of the Policy is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration statement identifying the constituent documents; each component is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section XVI(B)'s entire-agreement clause and the Section IV definition of 'Policy', with only a minor difference in whether the Application is included.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate consideration recital for a declarations amendment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the rest of the instrument pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two precise date ranges; the only interpretive question is the one-month extension, which is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The extension interacts with the 'Policy Year' definition (c056), which says an extension forms part of the Policy Year that would have ended on the original expiration date — a rule that has to be applied but does not contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of form numbers with no ambiguous language of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The list differs from the original Item 13 (c017) and from the name-change amendment (c026), so the operative endorsement schedule varies between documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 04/13/2009 is the original expiration date, consistent with the extension it effects.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard savings language, self-limiting by 'other than as above stated'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the identical clauses in every other endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate recital for a name/address change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No tension with other provisions found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure list of entity names; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: By placing Vantus Bank first it silently changes who is the 'Named Insured' under c053 ('the first named entity'), which matters for cancellation, notice and Section XVI(D) authorisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of form numbers; nothing to construe internally.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits form 5082 that a later amendment lists, so the endorsement schedules across the three declarations documents are not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict with other dated endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard savings language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the same clause elsewhere; harmonises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same plain-language claims-made notice as the Declarations version; definite statements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section IX(A)(1) and the Limit of Liability provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration and reliance recital with the usual 'subject to all terms, conditions and limitations'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with Section XV's representations clause and the incorporation of the Application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A crisp three-element condition for coverage to attach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Declarations Item 8 shows a '$0' retention for Insuring Agreement (A), which arguably fails the literal 'retention ... set forth' requirement of this clause and Item 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except for Loss the Company pays as indemnification' can be read as excluding only amounts actually paid or also amounts indemnifiable, a recurring D&O argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section VII(B)(1)-(2) and Section VIII(A)(2), which deem indemnifiable Loss to fall under Insuring Agreement (B) whether or not paid, a slightly different test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Has agreed to or is legally permitted or required by law to indemnify' is a broad but conventional trigger, stated in the alternative and reasonably clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the retention rules in Section VII(B)(2) and the deeming rule in Section VIII(A)(2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short entity-coverage grant; the terms are all defined elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach is heavily cut back by the Section VI exclusions and the Securities Liability Exclusion endorsement, but those are express carve-outs rather than contradictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence withdraws coverage for 'any loss arising from any act or omission by' the estate or spouse, which largely swallows the grant that precedes it; the subparagraph numbering also runs 'a)' then '(2)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the definitions of Insured Person and Loss; no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the direction of the Company' is a factual condition that could be disputed, but the wording is otherwise conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted by three separate endorsements (Brokerage, Fiduciary, Securities), so its residual scope depends on reading those together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section both grants a right to purchase on 'cancels or nonrenews ... or if the Policy converts subject to Section XIII (C)(1)(b)' and bars notice of circumstances during the period; the conversion limiter is a narrow, contestable trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XIII(C)(2) says the occurrence of any of the conversion events — not just (C)(1)(b) — shall not affect the right to purchase the Discovery Period, which is a genuine internal inconsistency about eligibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All applications, attachments and materials submitted' for this or any predecessor policy is an open-ended catch-all whose boundary is hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Section XV's representations and severability provisions and with the 'Policy' definition; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long definition with an inclusive limb ('also includes ... without limitation') and a carve-out for FDIC-insured deposit advice, leaving the general/specific boundary arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used both to grant coverage (Brokerage endorsement) and to exclude it (Section V(B)), but the endorsement expressly deletes the exclusion, so the fit is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated list is followed by the general tail 'for a Wrongful Act including any appeal from such proceeding', and item (1) covers any 'oral demand', which is the sort of catch-all/specific tension courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with the notice provisions in Section X and the Single Claim rule, which use 'first made' consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line statutory definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Fiduciary endorsement's employment-law exclusion; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition draws a line by the 'inception date' for subsidiaries and adds bank subsidiaries 'subject to Section XII (B)'; the temporal cut is clear enough on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Discovery Period Activation replaces this definition (c005) and deletes Section XII entirely (c006), so the cross-reference and the operative definition of 'Company' during the Discovery Period do not sit easily together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses' is a standard but inherently elastic standard, and the salary/overhead carve-out is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section IX(B)(2) gives the Insurer the right to verify reasonableness and necessity, so the two provisions reinforce rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statute is misnamed ('Employment Retirement Income Security Act' rather than Employee Retirement Income Security Act), a mechanical slip that does not obscure the reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ERISA is used in the exclusion and the Fiduciary endorsement consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition carves out 'a Leased Employee or Independent Contractor', two capitalised terms that are never defined anywhere in the Policy, leaving the exclusion's boundary unfixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Employee' feeds the Insured Person definition and the ERISA/Fiduciary provisions, and the undefined carve-out terms appear nowhere else in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two precise triggers — appointment of a receiver/conservator and debtor-in-possession status — with little play in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the retention rules (VII(B)(1)(b)), the Insolvency Exclusion (VI(D)), the Conversion provision and Section XVI(I), and those provisions pull in opposite directions on whether receivership defeats or preserves coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line composite definition; unambiguous as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fiduciary endorsement (c152) replaces it with a broader definition including Employee Benefit Plans, so 'Insured' means different things in different parts of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of capacities including 'honorary or advisory director'; broad but each category is named rather than left to a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Wrongful Act definition's 'solely in the capacity as such' and the Insured vs. Insured exclusion, which is where any fight would actually land.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed enumerated list of five services with no general catch-all limb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Insurance Services Exclusion, which carves out credit life/disability insurance consistently with the Brokerage/Advisory definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Common nexus any fact, circumstance, situation, event, transaction or series of related facts' is famously elastic — almost anything can share a 'common nexus' with something.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the Single Claim rule, the Prior Notice exclusion and Section XII(C)(2), all of which apply it consistently even if its scope is vague.
